To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The thermodynamic analysis has shown that a NH 3 /H 2 O absorption cycle using a base as additive seems promising for applications using waste heat sources and the Einstein– Szilard cycle offers higher COP than a conventional NH 3 / H 2 O-AHP at high temperatures and low temperature lift.

the thermodynamic simulation has shown that the Einstein–Szildar process offers higher COPs and the Rojyey cycle offers higher COPs than conventional NH3/H20-AHP at higher generator temperatures and low lift temperature differences, but that a NH3/ H2O absorption cycle with a strong base as an additive is promising for applications using a low-grade heat source and the investigated AHT and the Einstein– Szilard process seem not to be competitive to conventional technologies at present.
a NH3-H2O absorption cycle with a strong base as an additive is the most promising process among the investigated processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a systematic analysis of the thermodynamic behavior of alternative AHP-processes with respect to their thermodynamic performance.
the development of new absorption heat pumping processes with high COPs and low environmental impact.

the development of alternative absorption heat pump cycles using natural working fluids, which can be applied for heat recovery and for the use of low grade heat sources in the temperature range between 30 °C and 100 °C.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the investigated processes have to be developed further and that the development and application of new working fluids and new processes has to be supported.
there is no single AHP-process, which is superior to the conventional NH3/H20 absorption process for every application.
the investigated AHP-processes are still in a very preliminary stage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thermodynamic simulation is an important tool for the design of alternative AHP-processes.
the use of natural working mixtures in an AHT-process and in the Rojey process seems to be promising and should be studied further.
the thermodynamic simulation is a useful tool for the investigation and the development of alternative absorption processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thermodynamic simulation is a powerful tool to analyze the thermodynamic behavior of AHP-processes and to compare the performance of different AHP-processes.
the thermodynamic simulations are a very useful tool in the design and optimization of AHP-processes.

the application of alternative working mixtures and working fluids in absorption heat pumping processes is a promising approach to improve the performance and reduce the environmental impact of these processes.
